title: onprem: airgap offline bundle - vendor rke2/suse-microos EFI + rollback tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds a production-ready offline bundle and vendoring flow for RKE2 on SUSE MicroOS with EFI boot support plus a small rollback tool to safely revert bundle/TUF updates. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private on air-gapped SUSE MicroOS clusters with RKE2 have reported EFI boot path and vendor image layout mismatches that caused installation failures and manual recovery; this PR standardizes the bundle layout, vendors necessary runtime images and TUF metadata, and adds a lightweight rollback command to restore a previous offline bundle snapshot. Changes include: new bundle manifest and layout under packaging/offline-bundles/rke2/suse-microos, vendor script improvements to fetch and verify images (scripts/vendor-deps.sh), Helm chart tweaks to surface EFI-compatible init containers and kernel args (installer/helm/charts/redwood/templates/efi-support.yaml), values file for airgap installs (installer/helm/redwood/values-airgap.yaml), rollback tooling and small Go utility (tools/rollback/rollback_tool.go), and documentation and e2e fixtures (docs/airgap/rke2-suse-efi.md, test/e2e/airgap/rke2_suse_e2e.yml). The description below summarizes acceptance criteria, testing, and upgrade guidance: bundle creation is deterministic (sha256), TUF metadata signing and verification happen in the vendor step, install succeeds on rke2 v1.28+ on MicroOS with EFI enabled, and the rollback tool can restore the previous TUF metadata and image set without requiring node reprovisioning. This is backward-compatible and is intended to be included in the next offline bundle release.
commits_summary: 1) vendor: add rke2/suse-microos bundle manifest and image list; 2) scripts: make vendor-deps idempotent and add TUF upload step; 3) helm: add efi-support template and values override for airgap; 4) tools: add rollback_tool with dry-run and apply modes; 5) docs: airgap installation guide and troubleshooting
